title: An Australian platform worker resumed work after voluntary reactivation and later received a formal access-restoration order
source_unit: One Australian platform worker and Fair Work Commission proceeding; adjudicated same-case remedy follow-up, not a population estimate

observations.period: 2025-04-08 to 2025-09-23; deactivation, reactivation, post-reactivation work, and formal order

access_restoration.value: Uber voluntarily reactivated access on 2025-05-19; the Full Bench later ordered reactivation

continued_work.value: more than 150 trips completed after reactivation by 2025-07-21

reported_lived_burden.value: The Full Bench record describes extreme stress, anxiety, feeling unsupported, significant income loss, and financial hardship during the interruption
reported_lived_burden.unit: case-level reported worker experience recorded in adjudication

post_reactivation_work_payment.value: Full Bench record states that the worker performed work and received payment from Uber after 2025-05-19
post_reactivation_work_payment.unit: ordinary post-reactivation work payment; amount and timing not disclosed

financial_remedy.value: The 2025-09-23 order required reinstatement on the same terms and deemed regular work performed from 2025-03-24 through 2025-05-19; lost-remuneration quantum remained open for party consultation
financial_remedy.unit: formal access-restoration order and separate lost-remuneration remedy stage; remedy payment not observed

observations.method: Read the primary Fair Work Commission Full Bench and merits records as a dated single-case sequence, preserving voluntary reactivation, subsequent trip activity, formal order, and the separate open lost-pay stage.
observations.uncertainty: The public record establishes a case-level account of stress, anxiety, lack of support, income loss, and financial hardship during the interruption and payment for post-reactivation work, but does not establish net earnings, expenses, the amount or receipt of separate lost-remuneration relief, account status after the trip count, profile or rating correction, alternative work, recurrence protection, anti-retaliation, household recovery, trust change, collective action, or exit. One Australian case cannot estimate platform incidence or typical remedy effectiveness.
observations.subgroup: Single case: Mohammad Shareef Hotak and Uber Driver Platform / Rasier Pacific
observations.counterinterpretation: The recorded stress, anxiety, income loss, and financial hardship show lived burden in one adjudicated case, but not a population rate or a measured household recovery path. More than 150 trips and payment for post-reactivation work show operational return and ordinary work compensation, not unconstrained choice, recovery of lost earnings, or durable protection. Continued platform use may reflect dependence or lack of alternatives; the later formal order shows voluntary reactivation did not settle the separate lost-remuneration question.

related_sources.claim: The Commission's October 2025 regulated-worker update confirms that Hotak was ordered to be reactivated on the same terms and that Uber was directed to restore pay lost during deactivation; it reports no quantum or payment receipt.

The official 2025-09-23 order, effective 2025-09-26, required reinstatement on the same terms and deemed regular work performed during the 2025-03-24 to 2025-05-19 interruption; it does not state a lost-pay amount or receipt.
The Full Bench merits record preserves the formal reactivation order, post-reactivation work/payment statement, and open lost-remuneration stage.
The official FWC bulletin summarizes the worker's reported stress, anxiety, lack of support, income loss, and financial hardship during deactivation, alongside reactivation and lost-pay stages.
The committed local memo records the dates, 150-plus trips, remedy stages, and boundary.

boundary: This comparative Australian case closes voluntary access restoration, subsequent observed work activity, and ordinary payment for post-reactivation work before and alongside a formal access-restoration order. It does not close lost-remuneration payment, net recovery, alternative work, durable protection, trust, collective action, or practical exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Existing committed local Hotak follow-up memo, targeted official decision URLs, and 2026-10-19 indexed public-record recheck; no bulk archive retained
